title: Prophylaxis
line: Ask what your opponent wants, and stop it first.

steps.text: Before each move, ask what your opponent wants. Here Black would like to bring the bishop out to pin your knight to your queen.
Stop it before it happens: push the pawn on h2 one square, so the bishop cannot go to g4 without being taken.
steps.after: Stopping a plan before it starts is prophylaxis. Black's knight attacks your bishop instead.

steps.text: Now you are Black. White's knight on d4 would like to jump to b5 and hit d6 and c7. The bishop on f1 eyes that square too.
Take that square away from them with a pawn: push the pawn on a7 one square.
steps.after: Now neither piece can use b5. This is the Najdorf Sicilian, built on that one quiet move.

steps.text: With that square covered, Black can take space in the center: push the pawn in front of your king two squares.
steps.after: The pawn chases the knight from the center.

summary: Before your move, ask what your opponent wants to do. Often the best move stops it before it starts.
